title.zh: 卷七十四 四夷附錄第三: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城
title.en: Volume 74: Appendix on the Four Barbarians 3 - Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Tujie, Tubo, Huihu, Yutian, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Tungusic tribes, Nanzhao Man, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa
title.raw: 卷七十四 四夷附錄第三: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城 Volume 74: Appendix on the Four Barbarians 3 - Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Tujie, Tubo, Huihu, Yutian, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Tungusic tribes, Nanzhao Man, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa

sentences.zh: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城

translations.literal: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turks, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turks, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, and Champa.

sentences.zh: 奚，本匈奴之別種。

translations.literal: The Xi were originally a separate branch of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were originally an offshoot of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 當唐之末，居陰涼川，在營府之西，幽州之西南，皆數百里。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang they dwelt on the Yinliang River, west of the camp prefecture and southwest of Youzhou, each several hundred li distant.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Tang they lived along the Yinliang River, several hundred li west of the frontier camp and southwest of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 有人馬二萬騎。

translations.literal: They had twenty thousand men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They could field twenty thousand mounted warriors.

sentences.zh: 分爲五部：一曰阿薈部，二曰啜米部，三曰粵質部，四曰奴皆部，五曰黑訖支部。

translations.literal: They were divided into five divisions: first the Ahui division, second the Chuomi division, third the Yuezhi division, fourth the Nujie division, and fifth the Heiqizhi division.
translations.idiomatic: They were split into five divisions: the Ahui, Chuomi, Yuezhi, Nujie, and Heiqizhi.

sentences.zh: 後徙居琵琶川，在幽州東北數百里。

translations.literal: Later they moved to dwell on the Pipa River, several hundred li northeast of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later they relocated to the Pipa River, several hundred li northeast of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 地多黑羊，馬嵒前蹄堅善走，其登山逐獸，下上如飛。

translations.literal: The land had many black sheep; their horses had hard forehooves and ran well; in climbing mountains to pursue game they went up and down like flying.
translations.idiomatic: Black sheep were plentiful there, and their horses had exceptionally tough forehooves and great speed; hunting in the mountains, they seemed to fly up and down the slopes.

sentences.zh: 契丹阿保機強盛，室韋、奚、霫皆服屬之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Abaoji grew powerful, the Shiwei, Xi, and Wuhuan Xi all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan leader Abaoji rose to power, the Shiwei, the Xi, and the Wuhuan Xi all came under his sway.

sentences.zh: 奚人常爲契丹守界上，而苦其苛虐，奚王去諸怨叛，以別部西徙媯州，依北山射獵，常采北山麝香、仁參賂劉守光以自托。

translations.literal: The Xi often guarded the frontier for the Khitan but suffered under their harsh oppression; the Xi king Quzhu, resentful, rebelled, took a separate division west to Gui Prefecture, relied on the northern mountains for hunting, and often gathered musk and ginseng from those mountains to bribe Liu Shouguang for protection.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were often made to guard the Khitan borderlands and groaned under their cruelty. King Quzhu of the Xi rebelled in anger, led a splinter group west to Gui Prefecture, and lived by hunting in the northern hills, regularly trading musk and ginseng from those slopes to Liu Shouguang in exchange for his patronage.

sentences.zh: 其族至數千帳，始分爲東、西奚。

translations.literal: His people reached several thousand tents, and for the first time they were divided into Eastern and Western Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His following grew to several thousand tents, and the Xi were first split into eastern and western branches.

sentences.zh: 去諸之族，頗知耕種，歲借邊民荒地種穄，秋熟則來獲，窖之山下，人莫知其處。

translations.literal: Quzhu's people were fairly skilled at farming; each year they borrowed waste land from border Chinese to plant millet, came to harvest when it ripened in autumn, and stored it in pits beneath the hills so that no one knew the locations.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhu's band had learned something of agriculture. Each year they sowed millet on abandoned plots borrowed from frontier settlers, returned in autumn to reap the crop, and cached the grain in hidden pits in the hills, whose locations outsiders could not find.

sentences.zh: 爨以平底瓦鼎，煮穄爲粥，以寒水解之而飲。

translations.literal: They cooked with flat-bottomed earthenware pots, boiled millet into porridge, dissolved it in cold water, and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: They cooked in flat-bottomed clay pots, boiling millet into gruel that they thinned with cold water before drinking.

sentences.zh: 去諸卒，子掃剌立。

translations.literal: When Quzhu died, his son Saoci succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Quzhu died, his son Saoci became chief.

sentences.zh: 莊宗破劉守光，賜掃剌姓李，更其名紹威。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong defeated Liu Shouguang, he granted Saoci the surname Li and changed his name to Shaowei.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuangzong overthrew Liu Shouguang, he gave Saoci the surname Li and the new name Shaowei.

sentences.zh: 紹威卒，子拽剌立。

translations.literal: When Shaowei died, his son Zhuaila succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei was succeeded by his son Zhuaila.

sentences.zh: 同光以後，紹威父子數遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: After the Tongguang era, Shaowei and his son repeatedly sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tongguang reign onward, father and son sent tribute missions again and again.

sentences.zh: 初，紹威娶契丹女舍利逐不魯之姊爲妻，後逐不魯叛亡入西奚，紹威納之。

translations.literal: At first Shaowei married as wife the elder sister of the Khitan woman Shelizhubulu; later Zhubulu rebelled and fled into the Western Xi, and Shaowei took her in.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei had first married the elder sister of the Khitan woman Shelizhubulu. When Zhubulu later defected to the Western Xi, Shaowei took her in as well.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入立，割幽州雁門以北入於契丹，是時紹威與逐不魯皆已死，耶律德光已立晉北歸，拽剌迎謁馬前，德光曰：「非爾罪也。

translations.literal: When the Jin Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, the lands north of Youzhou and Yanmen were ceded to the Khitan; by then Shaowei and Zhubulu were both dead. Yelü Deguang had enthroned Jin and was returning north; Zhuaila met him before his horse, and Deguang said, "It is not your crime."
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Jin founder took the throne, he ceded everything north of Youzhou and Yanmen Pass to the Khitan. Shaowei and Zhubulu were already dead. Yelü Deguang, having placed Jin on the throne, was riding north when Zhuaila greeted him at his stirrup. Deguang said, "The fault is not yours."

sentences.zh: 負我者，掃剌與逐不魯爾。

translations.literal: Those who wronged me are Saoci and Zhubulu."
translations.idiomatic: Those who betrayed me are Saoci and Zhubulu."

sentences.zh: 」乃發其墓，粉其骨而揚之。

translations.literal: He then opened their tombs, ground their bones to powder, and scattered them.
translations.idiomatic: He had their graves opened, their bones ground to dust, and the dust cast to the winds.

sentences.zh: 後德光滅晉，拽剌常以兵從。

translations.literal: Later, when Deguang destroyed Jin, Zhuaila often followed with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Deguang later destroyed Jin, Zhuaila regularly marched at the head of his warriors in support.

sentences.zh: 其後不復見於中國。

translations.literal: After that they were no longer seen in China.
translations.idiomatic: After that they disappear from the Chinese record.

sentences.zh: 自去諸徙媯州，自別爲西奚，而東奚在琵琶川者，亦爲契丹所並，不復能自見云。

translations.literal: From the time Quzhu moved to Gui Prefecture and separated as the Western Xi, the Eastern Xi who remained on the Pipa River were also absorbed by the Khitan and could no longer maintain their own identity.
translations.idiomatic: Once Quzhu resettled at Gui and the Western Xi stood apart, the Eastern Xi on the Pipa River were swallowed up by the Khitan as well, and neither branch could any longer assert itself independently.

sentences.zh: 吐渾，本號吐谷渾，或曰乞伏乾歸之苗裔。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun were originally called Tuyuhun in full, or are said to be descendants of Qifu Gangui.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun, originally known as the Tuyuhun in full, were said to descend from Qifu Gangui.

sentences.zh: 自後魏以來，名見中國，居於青海之上。

translations.literal: Since the Later Wei their name has appeared in China; they dwelt above Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Their name had been known in China since the Northern Wei, when they lived beyond Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 當唐至德中，爲吐蕃所攻，部族分散，其內附者，唐處之河西。

translations.literal: In the Tang Zhide era they were attacked by Tibet; their tribes scattered, and those who submitted inward were settled by Tang in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang Zhide reign they were overrun by Tibet, their clans scattered, and those who submitted were resettled by the Tang in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其大姓有慕容、拓拔、赫連等族。

translations.literal: Their great clans included the Murong, Tuoba, Helian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Prominent lineages among them included the Murong, Tuoba, and Helian.

sentences.zh: 懿宗時，首領赫連鐸爲陰山府都督，與討龐勳，以功拜大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yizong's time the leader Helian Duo was commander of Yinshan Prefecture, joined the campaign against Pang Xun, and for merit was appointed military commissioner of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yizong, the chief Helian Duo served as commander of Yinshan Prefecture, helped suppress Pang Xun's rebellion, and was rewarded with the post of military commissioner of Datong.

sentences.zh: 爲晉王所破，其部族益微，散處蔚州界中。

translations.literal: He was defeated by the Prince of Jin, and their tribes grew ever weaker, scattered within the borders of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated by the Prince of Jin, the people grew weaker still and were scattered along the Yuzhou frontier.

sentences.zh: 莊宗時，有首領白承福者，依中山北石門爲柵，莊宗爲置寧朔、奉化兩府，以承福爲都督，賜其姓名爲李紹魯。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhuangzong's time there was a leader Bai Chengfu who relied on Shimen north of Zhongshan as a stockade; Zhuangzong established for him the two prefectures Ningshuo and Fenghua, made Chengfu commander, and granted him the surname and personal name Li Shaolu.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhuangzong's reign a leader named Bai Chengfu fortified Shimen north of Zhongshan. Zhuangzong created the Ningshuo and Fenghua prefectures for his people, appointed Chengfu their commander, and bestowed the Chinese name Li Shaolu.

sentences.zh: 終唐時，常遣使朝貢中國。

translations.literal: Throughout Tang they often sent envoys to offer tribute to China.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tang they regularly sent tribute missions to the court.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖立，割雁門以北入於契丹，於是吐渾爲契丹役屬，而苦其苛暴。

translations.literal: When the Jin Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, the lands north of Yanmen were ceded to the Khitan; the Tuyuhun then served the Khitan and suffered under their harsh cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin founder took power and ceded everything north of Yanmen to the Khitan, the Tuyuhun fell under Khitan domination and endured their brutal rule.

sentences.zh: 是時，安重榮鎮成德，有異志，陰遣人招吐渾入塞，承福等乃自五台入處中國。

translations.literal: At that time An Chongrong held Chengde and harbored rebellious designs; he secretly sent men to summon the Tuyuhun into the frontier, and Chengfu and others entered China from Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong, then military governor of Chengde, was plotting treason and secretly invited the Tuyuhun across the border. Chengfu and his followers came in from Wutai and settled within China.

sentences.zh: 契丹耶律德光大怒，遣使者責誚高祖，高祖恐懼，遣供奉官張澄率兵搜索並、鎮、忻、代等州山谷中吐渾驅出之。

translations.literal: The Khitan Yelü Deguang was greatly angered and sent envoys to rebuke Gaozu; Gaozu, afraid, sent the palace attendant Zhang Cheng with troops to search the valleys of Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai prefectures and drive the Tuyuhun out.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Deguang flew into a rage and sent envoys to upbraid the Jin emperor, who in fear dispatched the palace attendant Zhang Cheng to scour the hills of Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai and expel every Tuyuhun he could find.

sentences.zh: 然晉亦苦契丹，思得吐渾爲緩急之用，陰遣劉知遠鎮太原慰撫之。

translations.literal: Yet Jin also suffered from the Khitan and wished to keep the Tuyuhun for emergencies; they secretly sent Liu Zhiyuan to garrison Taiyuan and console them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin itself was harried by the Khitan and wanted the Tuyuhun as allies in a crisis, so it quietly posted Liu Zhiyuan at Taiyuan to win them over.

sentences.zh: 終高祖時，承福數遣使者朝貢。

translations.literal: Throughout Gaozu's reign Chengfu repeatedly sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of Gaozu's reign Chengfu sent tribute missions again and again.

sentences.zh: 後出帝與契丹絕盟，召承福入朝，拜大同軍節度使，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Chudi broke the alliance with the Khitan, he summoned Chengfu to court, appointed him military commissioner of Datong, and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chudi later renounced the Khitan alliance, he summoned Chengfu to court, made him military commissioner of Datong, and lavished favors on him.

sentences.zh: 契丹與晉相距於河，承福以其兵從出帝禦虜。

translations.literal: The Khitan and Jin faced each other across the Yellow River; Chengfu followed Chudi with his troops to resist the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: As Khitan and Jin armies confronted each other along the Yellow River, Chengfu marched with his warriors to aid Chudi against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 是歲大熱，吐渾多疾死，乃遣承福歸太原，居之嵐、石之間。

translations.literal: That year was intensely hot and many Tuyuhun died of illness; Chudi then sent Chengfu back to Taiyuan to dwell between Lan and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: That summer was punishingly hot, and disease carried off many Tuyuhun. Chudi sent Chengfu back to Taiyuan to settle his people between Lan and Shi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠稍侵辱之，承福謀復亡出塞，知遠以兵圍其族，殺承福及其大姓赫連海龍、白可久、白鐵匱等，其羊馬貲財巨萬計，皆籍沒之，其餘衆以其別部王義宗主之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan gradually insulted and humiliated them; Chengfu plotted to flee beyond the frontier again, and Zhiyuan surrounded his people with troops, killing Chengfu and the great clansmen Helian Hailong, Bai Kejiu, Bai Tiegui, and others; their sheep, horses, and goods numbering in the tens of thousands were all confiscated, and the remaining multitude was placed under Wang Yizong of another division.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan began to bully them. When Chengfu planned another escape beyond the passes, Zhiyuan surrounded the tribe, executed Chengfu and leading clansmen such as Helian Hailong, Bai Kejiu, and Bai Tiegui, seized their vast herds and wealth for the state treasury, and left the survivors under Wang Yizong of a collateral branch.

sentences.zh: 吐渾遂微，不復見。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun thus dwindled and were seen no more.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun thereafter faded from view.

sentences.zh: 初，唐以承福之族爲熟吐渾。

translations.literal: Earlier Tang had regarded Chengfu's people as the "ripe" Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang had earlier classified Chengfu's band as the acculturated, or "ripe," Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 長興中，又有生吐渾杜每兒來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era there also came to offer tribute Du Meier of the "raw" Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing reign a leader of the wild, or "raw," Tuyuhun named Du Meier also came to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 每兒，不知其國地、部族。

translations.literal: As for Meier, their homeland and tribal affiliation are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is known of Meier's homeland or clan affiliation.

sentences.zh: 至漢乾祐二年，又有吐渾何戛剌來朝貢，不知爲生、熟吐渾，蓋皆微，不足考錄。

translations.literal: By the second year of Qianyou in Han, another Tuyuhun named He Gela came to offer tribute; whether he was raw or ripe Tuyuhun is unknown—they were all so weak as to be unworthy of full record.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Later Han's Qianyou reign yet another Tuyuhun envoy, He Gela, arrived with tribute. Whether these visitors were raw or ripe Tuyuhun cannot be told; all were too insignificant to warrant fuller notice.

sentences.zh: 達靼，靺鞨之遺種，本在奚、契丹之東北，後爲契丹所攻，而部族分散，或屬契丹，或屬渤海，別部散居陰山者，自號達靼。

translations.literal: The Dada were a remnant stock of the Mohe, originally northeast of the Xi and Khitan; later attacked by the Khitan, their tribes scattered—some submitting to the Khitan, some to Bohai—while separate divisions dwelling scattered in the Yinshan range called themselves Dada.
translations.idiomatic: The Dada were descendants of the Mohe who once lived northeast of the Xi and Khitan. After Khitan attacks broke them apart, some bands joined the Khitan and others Bohai, while splinter groups along the Yinshan Mountains took the name Dada for themselves.

sentences.zh: 當唐末，以名見中國。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang their name appeared in China.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Tang their name was on record in China.

sentences.zh: 有每相溫、于越相溫，咸通中，從硃邪赤心討龐勳。

translations.literal: There were Meixiangwen and Yuyuexiangwen; in the Xiantong era they followed Zhuye Chixin in campaigning against Pang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Leaders named Meixiangwen and Yuyuexiangwen joined Zhuye Chixin's campaign against Pang Xun in the Xiantong period.

sentences.zh: 其後李國昌、克用父子爲赫連鐸等所敗，嘗亡入達靼。

translations.literal: Later Li Guochang and his son Keyong were defeated by Helian Duo and others and once fled into the Dada.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Guochang and his son Keyong were routed by Helian Duo and his allies, they took refuge among the Dada.

sentences.zh: 後從克用入關破黃巢，由是居雲、代之間。

translations.literal: Later they followed Keyong east of the passes to defeat Huang Chao and thereafter dwelt between Yun and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: They later marched with Keyong through the passes to crush Huang Chao and thereafter settled between Yun and Dai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其俗善騎射，畜多駝、馬。

translations.literal: Their custom favored mounted archery, and their herds were mostly camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled at mounted archery and raised great numbers of camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 其君長、部族名字，不可究見，惟其嘗通於中國者可見云。

translations.literal: The names of their chiefs and tribes cannot be fully traced; only those who had dealings with China can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Most of their chiefs and tribal names are lost to us; only those who had contact with China appear in the record.

sentences.zh: 同光中，都督折文逋數自河西來貢駝、馬。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era the commander Zhe Wenyu repeatedly came from Hexi to offer tribute of camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang reign the commander Zhe Wenyu made repeated missions from Hexi bearing camels and horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 明宗討王都於定州，都誘契丹入寇，明宗詔達靼入契丹界，以張軍勢，遣宿州刺史薛敬忠以所獲契丹團牌二百五十及弓箭數百賜雲州生界達靼，蓋唐常役屬之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong campaigned against Wang Du at Dingzhou, Du induced the Khitan to invade; Mingzong ordered the Dada into Khitan territory to inflate his army's strength and sent Suzhou prefect Xue Jingzhong to bestow on the Dada of Yunzhou's outer marches two hundred fifty Khitan round shields captured in battle and several hundred bows and arrows—for Tang had long used them as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong attacked Wang Du at Dingzhou, Du drew Khitan raiders into the war. Mingzong ordered Dada bands into Khitan territory to swell his front, and sent the prefect of Suzhou, Xue Jingzhong, to reward the frontier Dada of Yunzhou with two hundred fifty captured Khitan round shields and hundreds of bows and arrows—Tang had long treated them as auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 長興三年，首領頡哥率其族四百餘人來附。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changxing the leader Xiege led more than four hundred of his people to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing the chief Xiege brought more than four hundred followers to submit.

sentences.zh: 訖于顯德，常來不絕。

translations.literal: Down to Xiande they came without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions continued without interruption through the Xiande era.

sentences.zh: 党項，西羌之遺種。

translations.literal: The Tangut were a remnant stock of the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut were descendants of the Western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 其國在《禹貢》析支之地，東至松州，西接葉護，南界春桑，北鄰吐渾，有地三千餘里。

translations.literal: Their country lay in the Qizhi region of the "Tribute of Yu," east to Songzhou, west adjoining Yehu, south bordering Chunsang, north neighboring Tuyuhun, with territory of more than three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Their homeland lay in the Qizhi country described in the Tribute of Yu, reaching east to Songzhou, west to Yehu, south to Chunsang, and north to the Tuyuhun, spanning more than three thousand li.

sentences.zh: 無城邑而有室屋，以毛罽覆之。

translations.literal: They had no walled cities but had dwellings covered with felt.
translations.idiomatic: They built no walled towns, only felt-covered dwellings.

sentences.zh: 其人喜盜竊而多壽，往往百五六十歲。

translations.literal: Their people delighted in theft and lived long, often to one hundred fifty or sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: They were prone to raiding yet remarkably long-lived, often reaching one hundred fifty or sixty years of age.

sentences.zh: 其大姓有細封氏、費聽氏、折氏、野利氏，拓拔氏爲最強。

translations.literal: Their great clans included the Xifeng, Feiting, Zhe, and Yeli; the Tuoba were strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Major lineages included the Xifeng, Feiting, Zhe, and Yeli, with the Tuoba the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 唐德宗時，党項諸部相率內附，居慶州者號東山部落，居夏州者號平夏部落。

translations.literal: In Emperor Dezong's time the Tangut tribes submitted inward in succession; those dwelling in Qingzhou were called the Eastern Mountain tribes, those in Xiazhou the Pingxia tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong the Tangut tribes submitted in succession. Those around Qingzhou were called the Eastern Mountain tribes; those around Xiazhou, the Pingxia tribes.

sentences.zh: 部有大姓而無君長，不相統一，散處邠寧、鄜延、靈武、河西，東至麟、府之間。

translations.literal: The tribes had great clans but no single chief, were not unified, and were scattered through Binning, Fuyan, Lingwu, and Hexi, east to between Lin and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: They recognized great clan names but no paramount ruler, remained divided, and were scattered from Binning and Fuyan through Lingwu and Hexi as far east as Lin and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 自同光以後，大姓之強者各自來朝貢。

translations.literal: From the Tongguang era onward, the powerful great clans each came to offer tribute on their own.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tongguang reign each powerful clan sent its own tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，詔沿邊置場市馬，諸夷皆入市中國，而回鶻、党項馬最多。

translations.literal: In Mingzong's time an edict established frontier markets for horses; all the barbarians entered China to trade, and Uyghur and Tangut horses were most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong ordered horse markets set up along the frontier. Tribal traders flocked to China, with Uyghur and Tangut horses the most common.

sentences.zh: 明宗招懷遠人，馬來無駑壯皆售，而所售常過直，往來館給，道路倍費。

translations.literal: Mingzong sought to win over distant peoples; every horse that came, whether weak or strong, was bought, and the price paid often exceeded fair value; lodging and provisions on the road doubled the expense.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong courted distant peoples by buying every horse offered, sound or sorry, often above market price, while lodging and travel costs along the route doubled the burden.

sentences.zh: 其每至京師，明宗爲御殿見之，勞以酒食，既醉，連袂歌呼，道其土風以爲樂，去又厚以賜賚，歲耗百萬計。

translations.literal: Whenever they reached the capital, Mingzong received them in the imperial hall, entertained them with food and wine, and once drunk they linked arms singing and shouting, telling of their native customs for amusement; on departure he again gave lavish gifts, costing millions each year.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they reached the capital, Mingzong received them in the palace, feasted them with food and wine, and watched them, arm in arm and roaring songs, perform their homeland customs for sport. Lavish parting gifts followed, draining more than a million strings of cash a year.

sentences.zh: 唐大臣皆患之，數以爲言。

translations.literal: Tang ministers all regarded this as a affliction and repeatedly spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers deplored the expense and remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 乃詔吏就邊場售馬給直，止其來朝，而党項利其所得，來不可止。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered officials to buy horses and pay fair price at the frontier markets and stop their coming to court—but the Tangut profited from what they gained and could not be stopped from coming.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then directed officials to buy horses at fair prices on the frontier and barred further court visits. The Tangut, however, prized their profits and kept coming anyway.

sentences.zh: 其在靈、慶之間者，數犯邊爲盜。

translations.literal: Those between Ling and Qing repeatedly raided the frontier as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Bands between Ling and Qing prefectures raided the border again and again.

sentences.zh: 自河西回鶻朝貢中國，道其部落，輒邀劫之，執其使者，賣之他族，以易牛馬。

translations.literal: Since the Hexi Uyghurs came to offer tribute to China, whenever their route passed Tangut territory they were ambushed; their envoys were seized and sold to other tribes to exchange for cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hexi Uyghur tribute missions passed through Tangut lands, the Tangut ambushed them, seized the envoys, and sold them to other tribes for cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣靈武康福、邠州藥彥稠等出兵討之。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent Kang Fu of Lingwu, Yao Yanchou of Binzhou, and others with troops to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong dispatched Kang Fu of Lingwu, Yao Yanchou of Binzhou, and others to punish them.

sentences.zh: 福等擊破阿埋韋悉褒勒強賴埋廝骨尾及其大首領連香李八薩王、都統悉那埋摩、侍御乞埋嵬悉逋等族，殺數千人，獲其牛羊巨萬計，及其所劫外國寶玉等，悉以賜軍士。

translations.literal: Fu and the others defeated the tribes of Amai, Weixi, Baole, Qianglaimai, Siguwei, and their great chiefs Lianxiang, Li Basawang, the commander-in-chief Xinamaimo, the attendant Qimai Weixibo, and others, killing several thousand; they captured tens of thousands of their sheep and cattle and the foreign gems and jades they had plundered, all given to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's forces crushed the Amai, Weixi, Baole, Qianglaimai, and Siguwei clans along with chiefs such as Lianxiang, Li Basawang, Commander-in-Chief Xinamaimo, and Attendant Qimai Weixibo, killing thousands. Vast herds and the foreign gems they had looted were distributed among the troops.

sentences.zh: 由是党項之患稍息。

translations.literal: Thus the Tangut menace eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut raids thereafter subsided for a time.

sentences.zh: 至周太祖時，府州党項尼也六泥香王子、拓拔山等皆來朝貢。

translations.literal: By the time of the Zhou Emperor Taizu, the Fuzhou Tangut Niyeliuni Xiangwangzi, Tuobashan, and others all came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou founder, Fuzhou Tangut leaders such as Niyeliuni Xiangwangzi and Tuobashan came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年，慶州刺史郭彥欽貪其羊馬，侵擾諸部，獨野雞族強不可近，乃誣其族犯邊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun the Qingzhou prefect Guo Yanqin, greedy for their sheep and horses, harassed the tribes; only the Yaji clan was strong and could not be approached, so he falsely accused them of raiding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun the prefect of Qingzhou, Guo Yanqin, coveting their herds, bullied the tribes. Only the Yaji clan remained too formidable to bully, so he falsely accused them of border raids.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使招慰之。

translations.literal: Taizu sent envoys to console and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent envoys to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 野雞族苦彥欽，不肯聽命，太祖遣邠州折從阮、甯州刺史張建武等討之。

translations.literal: The Yaji clan, suffering under Yanqin, refused to obey; Taizu sent Zhe Congruan of Binzhou, Zhang Jianwu the prefect of Ningzhou, and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Harried by Yanqin, the Yaji refused to submit. Taizu dispatched Zhe Congruan of Binzhou and Zhang Jianwu of Ningzhou to attack them.

sentences.zh: 建武勇於立功，不能通夷情，馳軍擊野雞族，殺數百人。

translations.literal: Jianwu was eager for merit but did not understand barbarian sentiment; he charged his army against the Yaji and killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Eager for glory but ignorant of tribal ways, Jianwu charged the Yaji and killed several hundred.

sentences.zh: 而喜玉、折思、殺牛三族聞建武擊破野雞族，各以牛酒犒軍，軍士利其物，反劫掠之。

translations.literal: When the Xiyu, Zhesi, and Shaniu clans heard that Jianwu had broken the Yaji, each brought cattle and wine to reward the army; the soldiers coveted their goods and instead plundered them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiyu, Zhesi, and Shaniu clans, hearing of the victory, brought cattle and wine to feast the troops. The soldiers coveted the gifts and looted the donors instead.

sentences.zh: 三族共誘建武軍至包山，度險，三族共擊之，軍投崖谷，死傷甚衆。

translations.literal: The three clans together lured Jianwu's army to Baoshan; crossing the dangerous terrain, they jointly attacked, and the army tumbled into cliffs and ravines with very many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The three clans lured Jianwu's force to Baoshan, ambushed them in the defiles, and drove many soldiers over the cliffs to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，罪建武等，選良吏爲慶州刺史以招撫之。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry and punished Jianwu and the others, selecting capable officials as Qingzhou prefect to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu punished Jianwu and his officers and appointed able men as prefect of Qingzhou to pacify the tribes.

sentences.zh: 其他諸族，散處尚邊界上者甚衆，然其無國地、君長，故莫得而紀次云。

translations.literal: Other tribes scattered along the frontier were very numerous, yet because they had no fixed territory or chief, they cannot be recorded in order.
translations.idiomatic: Countless other tribes still dotted the frontier, but without fixed territories or rulers they cannot be set down in any orderly account.

sentences.zh: 突厥，國地、君世、部族、名號、物俗，見於唐著矣。

translations.literal: The Turks—their territory, rulers, tribes, titles, and customs—are fully recorded in Tang histories.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks' lands, rulers, tribes, titles, and customs were already set forth in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 至唐之末。

translations.literal: By the end of Tang
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Tang

sentences.zh: 爲諸夷所侵，部族微散。

translations.literal: they were invaded by the various barbarians and their tribes dwindled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: they had been harried by neighboring peoples until their clans were broken and scattered.

sentences.zh: 五代之際，嘗來朝貢。

translations.literal: During the Five Dynasties they sometimes came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties period they still sent occasional tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，渾解樓來。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang Hun Jielou came.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang, Hun Jielou arrived.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，首領張慕晉來。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng the leader Zhang Mujin came.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng the chief Zhang Mujin came.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，首領杜阿熟來。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing the leader Du Ashu came.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing the chief Du Ashu came.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，遣使者薛同海等來。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu they sent envoys Xue Tonghai and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu they dispatched envoys led by Xue Tonghai.

sentences.zh: 凡四至，其後不復來。

translations.literal: They came four times in all; afterward they came no more.
translations.idiomatic: They came four times in all, then ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 然突厥于時最微，又來不數，故其君長史皆失不能紀。

translations.literal: Yet the Turks were then weakest of all and came but rarely, so the histories of their chiefs are lost and cannot be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Turks were the weakest of peoples and visited but seldom, so the names and deeds of their chiefs have been lost.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃，國地、君世、部族、名號、物俗，見於唐著矣。

translations.literal: Tibet—their territory, rulers, tribes, titles, and customs—are fully recorded in Tang histories.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet's lands, rulers, tribes, titles, and customs were already set forth in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 當唐之盛時，河西、隴右三十三州，涼州最大，土沃物繁而人富樂。

translations.literal: When Tang was at its height, Hexi and Longyou had thirty-three prefectures; Liangzhou was largest, its soil fertile, its goods abundant, its people wealthy and content.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of Tang power, Hexi and Longyou comprised thirty-three prefectures. Liangzhou was the greatest: fertile soil, rich produce, and a prosperous, contented population.

sentences.zh: 其地宜馬，唐置八監，牧馬三十萬匹。

translations.literal: The land suited horses; Tang established eight stud farms and pastured three hundred thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The region was ideal for horses; the Tang maintained eight stud farms pasturing three hundred thousand mounts.

sentences.zh: 以安西都護府羈縻西域三十六國。

translations.literal: Through the Protectorate General of Anxi they kept the thirty-six states of the Western Regions in loose allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Protectorate General of Anxi the court held the thirty-six states of the Western Regions in loose allegiance.

sentences.zh: 唐之軍、鎮、監、務，三百餘城，常以中國兵更戍，而涼州置使節度之。

translations.literal: Tang armies, garrisons, stud farms, and supply posts numbered more than three hundred cities; Chinese troops were regularly rotated to garrison them, and a commissioner was stationed at Liangzhou to command the region.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred Tang garrisons, stud farms, and supply posts dotted the region, manned by rotating Chinese troops under a commissioner stationed at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山之亂，肅宗起靈武，悉召河西兵赴難，而吐蕃乘虛攻陷河西、隴右，華人百萬皆陷於虜。

translations.literal: In An Lushan's rebellion, Emperor Suzong rose at Lingwu and summoned all Hexi troops to the rescue; Tibet seized the opportunity to attack and capture Hexi and Longyou, and a million Chinese subjects fell captive to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Suzong rallied at Lingwu and called every Hexi soldier east to the rescue. Tibet struck the undefended west, overran Hexi and Longyou, and a million Chinese subjects fell into Tibetan hands.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，嘗遣使者至西域，見甘、涼、瓜、沙等州城邑如故，而陷虜之人見唐使者，夾道迎呼，涕泣曰：「皇帝猶念陷蕃人民否？

translations.literal: In Emperor Wenzong's time envoys were once sent to the Western Regions and found the cities of Gan, Liang, Guazhou, Shazhou and the like still as before; when those who had fallen captive saw the Tang envoys, they lined the roads to welcome and call out, weeping and saying, "Does the Emperor still remember the people who fell to Tibet?"
translations.idiomatic: During Wenzong's reign envoys reached the western lands and found Gan, Liang, Guazhou, Shazhou, and the other prefectures still standing as before. Subjects trapped in Tibetan hands lined the roads to greet the Tang emissaries, weeping as they cried, "Does the Son of Heaven still remember those of us lost to Tibet?"

sentences.zh: 」其人皆天寶時陷虜者子孫，其語言稍變，而衣服猶不改。

translations.literal: Those people were all descendants of captives from the Tianbao era; their speech had changed somewhat, but their clothing had not.
translations.idiomatic: They were all descendants of subjects taken captive in the Tianbao reign. Their speech had shifted, but they still dressed as Chinese.

sentences.zh: 至五代時，吐蕃已微弱，回鶻、党項諸羌夷分侵其地，而不有其人民。

translations.literal: By the Five Dynasties Tibet had grown weak; Uyghurs, Tangut, and various Qiang barbarians divided and invaded its lands but did not hold its people.
translations.idiomatic: By the Five Dynasties period Tibet had weakened. Uyghurs, Tangut, and other Qiang peoples carved up its territory but could not rule its population.

sentences.zh: 值中國衰亂，不能撫有，惟甘、涼、瓜、沙四州常自通於中國。

translations.literal: China was in decline and turmoil and could not govern them; only the four prefectures Gan, Liang, Guazhou, and Shazhou regularly maintained contact with China on their own.
translations.idiomatic: With China in turmoil the court could no longer govern the region, yet Gan, Liang, Guazhou, and Shazhou still kept contact with the capital on their own.

sentences.zh: 甘州爲回鶻牙，而涼、瓜、沙三州將吏，猶稱唐官，數來請命。

translations.literal: Ganzhou was the Uyghur headquarters, while the officers of Liang, Guazhou, and Shazhou still called themselves Tang officials and repeatedly came to request commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou served as the Uyghur headquarters, while officers in Liang, Guazhou, and Shazhou still styled themselves Tang officials and repeatedly petitioned for imperial commissions.

sentences.zh: 自梁太祖時，嘗以靈武節度使兼領河西節度，而觀察甘、肅、威等州。

translations.literal: From the time of the Liang Emperor Taizu, the military governor of Lingwu was sometimes also made governor of Hexi and overseer of Gan, Su, Wei, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: From the Liang founder's reign onward the Lingwu military governor sometimes also held the Hexi command and oversaw Gan, Su, Wei, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 然雖有其名，而涼州自立守將。

translations.literal: Yet though the title existed in name, Liangzhou maintained its own defending generals.
translations.idiomatic: In name the office existed, but Liangzhou kept its own local defenders.

sentences.zh: 唐長興四年，涼州留後孫超遣大將拓拔承謙及僧、道士、耆老楊通信等至京師求旌節，明宗問孫超等世家，承謙曰：「吐蕃陷涼州，張掖人張義朝募兵擊走吐蕃，唐因以義朝爲節度使，發鄆州兵二千五百人戍之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing of Tang, the acting prefect of Liangzhou Sun Chao sent the great general Tuoba Chengqian and monks, Daoist priests, and elder Yang Tongxin and others to the capital to request a commission; Mingzong asked about Sun Chao's lineage, and Chengqian said, "When Tibet captured Liangzhou, Zhang Yichao of Zhangye raised troops and drove the Tibetans away; Tang therefore made Yichao military commissioner and sent twenty-five hundred troops from Yanzhou to garrison it."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing, acting prefect Sun Chao of Liangzhou sent General Tuoba Chengqian, monks, Daoist priests, and elder Yang Tongxin to the capital to request an imperial commission. When Mingzong asked about Sun Chao's background, Chengqian replied, "After Tibet seized Liangzhou, Zhang Yichao of Zhangye raised troops and drove them out. The Tang appointed Yichao military commissioner and sent twenty-five hundred men from Yanzhou to garrison the city."

sentences.zh: 唐亡，天下亂，涼州以東爲突厥、党項所隔，鄆兵遂留不得返。

translations.literal: When Tang fell and the realm was in chaos, the lands east of Liangzhou were cut off by Turks and Tangut, and the Yanzhou garrison could not return.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang fell and the realm dissolved into chaos, Turks and Tangut blocked the route east, and the Yanzhou garrison was stranded.

sentences.zh: 今涼州漢人，皆其戍人子孫也。

translations.literal: The Chinese of Liangzhou today are all descendants of those garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese population of Liangzhou today are all descendants of those garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 」明宗乃拜孫超節度使。

translations.literal: Mingzong then appointed Sun Chao military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong then appointed Sun Chao military commissioner of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，留後李文謙來請命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai the acting prefect Li Wenqian came to request a commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingtai, acting prefect Li Wenqian petitioned for a commission.

sentences.zh: 後數年，涼州人逐出文謙，靈武馮暉遣牙將吳繼勳代文謙爲留後，是時天福七年。

translations.literal: Several years later the people of Liangzhou drove Wenqian out; Feng Hui of Lingwu sent his officer Wu Jixun to replace Wenqian as acting prefect—this was the seventh year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later the people of Liangzhou expelled Wenqian. Feng Hui of Lingwu sent his officer Wu Jixun to replace him as acting prefect in the seventh year of Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 明年，晉高祖遣涇州押牙陳延暉齎詔書安撫涼州，涼州人共劫留延暉，立以爲刺史。

translations.literal: The next year the Jin Emperor Gaozu sent Chen Yanhui, adjutant of Jingzhou, bearing an edict to console Liangzhou; the people of Liangzhou together detained Yanhui by force and installed him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jin Gaozu sent Jingzhou adjutant Chen Yanhui with an edict to pacify Liangzhou. The locals seized him and made him their prefect.

sentences.zh: 至漢隱帝時，涼州留後折逋嘉施來請命，漢即以爲節度使。

translations.literal: By the time of the Han Emperor Yindi, the acting prefect of Liangzhou Zhebo Jiashi came to request a commission, and Han immediately appointed him military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han's Emperor Yindi, acting prefect Zhebo Jiashi of Liangzhou petitioned for a commission and was appointed military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉施，土豪也。

translations.literal: Jiashi was a local strongman.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashi was a local magnate.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，嘉施遣人市馬京師，因來請命帥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, Jiashi sent men to trade horses in the capital and thereby came to request appointment as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun, Jiashi sent agents to sell horses in the capital and used the occasion to request formal command of the region.

sentences.zh: 是時，樞密使王峻用事。

translations.literal: At that time the commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jun held power.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Commissioner Wang Jun of the Bureau of Military Affairs dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 峻故人申師厚者，少起盜賊，爲兗州牙將，與峻相友善，後峻貴，師厚敝衣蓬首，日候峻出，拜馬前，訴以饑寒，峻未有以發。

translations.literal: Jun's old acquaintance Shen Shihou had risen from banditry in youth and served as an officer of Yanzhou; he and Jun were on friendly terms. After Jun grew eminent, Shihou in ragged clothes and unkempt hair daily waited for Jun to emerge, bowed before his horse, and complained of hunger and cold, but Jun had no way to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's old friend Shen Shihou had begun life as a bandit and became an officer in Yanzhou. When Jun rose to power, Shihou would wait for him each day in ragged clothes and matted hair, bow before his horse, and plead for relief from hunger and cold, yet Jun had nothing to give him.

sentences.zh: 而嘉施等來請帥，峻即建言：「涼州深入夷狄，中國未嘗命吏，請募率府率、供奉官能往者。

translations.literal: When Jiashi and others came to request a commander, Jun at once proposed: "Liangzhou lies deep among the barbarians; China has never appointed officials there. Let us recruit a commander of the guard or a palace attendant willing to go."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiashi's petition arrived, Jun proposed, "Liangzhou lies deep in barbarian country and China has never stationed officials there. Let us recruit a guard commander or palace attendant willing to take the post."

sentences.zh: 」月餘，無應募者，乃奏起師厚爲左衛將軍，已而拜河西節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a month with no volunteers, he memorialized to recall Shihou as general of the Left Guard, and shortly afterward appointed him military commissioner of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: After a month without volunteers, he had Shihou recalled as general of the Left Guard and soon appointed him military commissioner of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 師厚至涼州，奏薦押衙副使崔虎心、陽妃谷首領沈念般等及中國留人子孫王廷翰、溫崇樂、劉少英爲將吏。

translations.literal: When Shihou reached Liangzhou he memorialized recommending the deputy adjutant Cui Huxin, the Yangfeigu chief Shen Nianban, and descendants of Chinese who had remained—Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying—as officers.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Liangzhou, Shihou recommended adjutant Cui Huxin, Yangfeigu chief Shen Nianban, and descendants of stranded Chinese such as Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying for military posts.

sentences.zh: 又自安國鎮至涼州，立三州以控扼諸羌，用其酋豪爲刺史。

translations.literal: He also from Anguo garrison to Liangzhou established three prefectures to control the various Qiang, appointing their chieftains as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Between Anguo and Liangzhou he established three prefectures to restrain the Qiang tribes, appointing tribal chiefs as prefects.

sentences.zh: 然涼州夷夏雜處，師厚小人，不能撫有。

translations.literal: Yet Liangzhou was a mixed land of barbarians and Chinese; Shihou was a petty man and could not govern it.
translations.idiomatic: But Liangzhou was a mixed frontier of Chinese and tribesmen, and the petty Shihou could not hold it together.

sentences.zh: 至世宗時，師厚留其子而逃歸，涼州遂絕於中國。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Shizong, Shihou left his son behind and fled back; Liangzhou was then cut off from China.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong, Shihou abandoned his son and fled home. Liangzhou was lost to China thereafter.

sentences.zh: 獨瓜、沙二州，終五代常來。

translations.literal: Only Guazhou and Shazhou, throughout the Five Dynasties, came regularly.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guazhou and Shazhou maintained regular contact throughout the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 沙州，梁開平中有節度使張奉，自號「金山白衣天子」。

translations.literal: At Shazhou, in the Kaiping era of Liang there was a military commissioner Zhang Feng who styled himself "White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: At Shazhou during Liang's Kaiping era, military commissioner Zhang Feng styled himself the White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至唐莊宗時，回鶻來朝，沙州留後曹義金亦遣使附回鶻以來，莊宗拜義金爲歸義軍節度使、瓜沙等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: By the time of Tang Emperor Zhuangzong the Uyghurs came to court; the acting prefect of Shazhou Cao Yijin also sent envoys attached to the Uyghur mission, and Zhuangzong appointed Yijin military commissioner of the Army of Returning Allegiance and commissioner overseeing Guazhou, Shazhou, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs visited Zhuangzong's court, acting prefect Cao Yijin of Shazhou sent envoys in their train. Zhuangzong appointed Yijin commissioner of the Army of Returning Allegiance and overseer of Guazhou and Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年，義金卒，子元德立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin, Yijin died and his son Yuande succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yijin died in the fifth year of Tianfu and was succeeded by his son Yuande.

sentences.zh: 至七年，沙州曹元忠、瓜州曹元深皆遣使來。

translations.literal: By the seventh year, Cao Yuanzhong of Shazhou and Cao Yuanshen of Guazhou both sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Cao Yuanzhong of Shazhou and Cao Yuanshen of Guazhou both sent missions.

sentences.zh: 周世宗時，又以元忠爲歸義軍節度使，元恭爲瓜州團練使。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time Yuanzhong was again made military commissioner of the Army of Returning Allegiance and Yuangong regimental commissioner of Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou's Emperor Shizong, Yuanzhong was again made commissioner of the Army of Returning Allegiance and Yuangong regimental commissioner of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 其所貢：硇砂、羚羊角、波斯錦、安西白灊、金星礬、胡桐律、大鵬砂、毦褐、玉團。

translations.literal: Their tribute included sal ammoniac, antelope horns, Persian brocade, Anxi white felt, golden-star alum, tamarisk resin, great-peng sand, felt coats, and jade balls.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute included sal ammoniac, antelope horn, Persian brocade, Anxi white felt, golden-star alum, tamarisk resin, great-peng sand, felt coats, and jade spheres.

sentences.zh: 皆因其來者以名見，而其卒立、世次，史皆失其紀。

translations.literal: All are known only through those who came; their deaths, successions, and genealogies are lost in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: We know them only through the names of visiting envoys; the records of their deaths, successions, and lineages have been lost.

sentences.zh: 而吐蕃不見於梁世。

translations.literal: Tibet does not appear in the Liang era.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet does not appear in the records of the Liang.

sentences.zh: 唐天成三年，回鶻王仁喻來朝，吐蕃亦遣使附以來，自此數至中國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng of Tang the Uyghur king Renyu came to court; Tibet also sent envoys attached to them, and from then on they came repeatedly to China.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng the Uyghur king Renyu came to court, and Tibet sent envoys in his train. Thereafter Tibetan missions reached China repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘗禦端明殿見其使者，問其牙帳所居，曰：「西去涇州二千里。

translations.literal: Mingzong once received their envoys in the Hall of Illustrious Clarity and asked where their headquarters lay; they said, "Two thousand li west of Jingzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong once received their envoys in the Hall of Illustrious Clarity and asked where their headquarters stood. They replied, "Two thousand li west of Jingzhou."

sentences.zh: 」明宗賜以虎皮，人一張，皆披以拜，委身宛轉，落其氈帽，亂髮如蓬，明宗及左右皆大笑。

translations.literal: Mingzong bestowed tiger skins, one per man; all draped them to bow, twisting their bodies in obeisance until their felt caps fell off and their tangled hair stood like rushes; Mingzong and his attendants all laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong gave each man a tiger skin. They draped the pelts to bow, writhing so violently that their felt caps fell off and their tangled hair flew like rushes, to the great amusement of the emperor and his attendants.

sentences.zh: 至漢隱帝時猶來朝，後遂不復至，史亦失其君世云。

translations.literal: They still came to court in the time of Han Emperor Yindi; afterward they came no more, and the histories have lost their rulers' genealogies.
translations.idiomatic: They still came under Later Han's Emperor Yindi, then ceased entirely, and the line of their rulers has been lost.

sentences.zh: 回鶻，爲唐患尤甚。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were an affliction to Tang above all others.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the peoples who troubled the Tang, the Uyghurs were the greatest menace.

sentences.zh: 其國地、君世、物俗，見於唐著矣。

translations.literal: Their territory, rulers, and customs are fully recorded in Tang histories.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands, rulers, and customs were already set forth in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 唐嘗以女妻之，故其世以中國爲舅。

translations.literal: Tang once gave them princesses in marriage, so their generations called China "uncle."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang had given them imperial brides, so they called China their uncle-by-marriage.

sentences.zh: 其國本在娑陵水上、後爲黠戛斯所侵，徙天德、振武之間，又爲石雄、張仲武所破，其餘衆西徙，役屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: Their state was originally on the Seling River; later, invaded by the Kirghiz, they moved between Tiande and Zhenwu; then defeated by Shi Xiong and Zhang Zhongwu, the remnant masses moved west and served Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: They had originally lived along the Seling River. After the Kirghiz drove them out, they shifted between Tiande and Zhenwu. Defeated by Shi Xiong and Zhang Zhongwu, the survivors moved west and submitted to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 是時吐蕃已陷河西、隴右，乃以回鶻散處之。

translations.literal: Tibet had then already captured Hexi and Longyou and scattered the Uyghurs to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had already seized Hexi and Longyou and settled the Uyghur remnants across that region.

sentences.zh: 當五代之際，有居甘州、西州者嘗見中國，而甘州回鶻數至，猶呼中國爲舅，中國答以詔書亦呼爲甥。

translations.literal: During the Five Dynasties those dwelling in Ganzhou and Xizhou sometimes appeared in China; the Ganzhou Uyghurs came frequently and still called China "uncle," and China in edicts called them "nephew."
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties the Uyghurs of Ganzhou and Xizhou still had contact with China. The Ganzhou Uyghurs came often, still calling China their uncle, while Chinese edicts addressed them as nephews.

sentences.zh: 梁乾化元年，遣都督周易言等來，而史不見其君長名號，梁拜易言等官爵，遣左監門衛上將軍楊沼押領還蕃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua of Liang they sent the commander Zhou Yiyan and others, but the histories do not record their ruler's name; Liang invested Yiyan and others with titles and sent Yang Zhao of the Left Gate Guard to escort them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianhua they sent Commander Zhou Yiyan and others, though the histories do not record their ruler's name. Liang granted Yiyan titles and sent Yang Zhao of the Left Gate Guard to escort the mission home.

sentences.zh: 至唐莊宗時，王仁美遣使者來，貢玉、馬，自稱「權知可汗」，莊宗遣司農卿鄭續持節冊仁美爲英義可汗。

translations.literal: By the time of Tang Emperor Zhuangzong, Wang Renmei sent envoys offering jade and horses, styling himself "acting khan"; Zhuangzong sent the minister of agriculture Zheng Xu with credentials to invest Renmei as the Yingyi Kaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong, Wang Renmei sent envoys with jade and horses, styling himself acting khan. Zhuangzong dispatched Minister of Agriculture Zheng Xu to invest him as the Yingyi Kaghan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，仁美卒，其弟狄銀立，遣都督安千想等來。

translations.literal: That year Renmei died; his brother Diyin succeeded and sent the commander An Qianxiang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Renmei died that year and was succeeded by his brother Diyin, who sent Commander An Qianxiang and others.

sentences.zh: 同光四年，狄銀卒，阿咄欲立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang Diyin died and Aduyu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Diyin died in the fourth year of Tongguang and was succeeded by Aduyu.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，權知國事王仁裕遣李阿山等來朝，明宗遣使者冊仁裕爲順化可汗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng Wang Renyu, acting in state affairs, sent Li Ashan and others to court; Mingzong sent envoys to invest Renyu as the Shunhua Kaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng, Wang Renyu, acting ruler, sent Li Ashan and others to court. Mingzong invested him as the Shunhua Kaghan.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時又冊爲奉化可汗。

translations.literal: In the time of Jin Emperor Gaozu he was again invested as the Fenghua Kaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Gaozu later invested him as the Fenghua Kaghan.

sentences.zh: 阿咄欲，不知其爲狄銀親疏，亦不知其立卒；

translations.literal: As for Aduyu, it is unknown how he was related to Diyin, or when he rose and died;
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is known of Aduyu's kinship to Diyin or the dates of his rise and death;

sentences.zh: 而仁裕訖五代常來朝貢，史亦失其紀。

translations.literal: but Renyu throughout the Five Dynasties came regularly with tribute, and the histories have lost his record as well.
translations.idiomatic: yet Renyu sent tribute throughout the Five Dynasties, and his line too has been lost from the record.

sentences.zh: 其地出玉、犛、綠野馬、獨峰駝、白貂鼠、羚羊角、硇砂、膃肭臍、金剛鑽、紅鹽、罽氎、騊駼之革。

translations.literal: Their land produced jade, yak, green wild horses, Bactrian camels, white sable, antelope horn, sal ammoniac, narwhal tusk, diamond drills, red salt, felt cloth, and taotu leather.
translations.idiomatic: Their country yielded jade, yak, green wild horses, Bactrian camels, white sable, antelope horn, sal ammoniac, narwhal tusk, diamond drills, red salt, felt cloth, and taotu leather.

sentences.zh: 其地宜白麥、青騑麥、黃麻、蔥韭、胡荽，以橐駝耕而種。

translations.literal: Their land suited white wheat, blue-green wheat, yellow hemp, scallions, leeks, and coriander, planted by plowing with camels.
translations.idiomatic: They grew white wheat, bluish wheat, yellow hemp, scallions, leeks, and coriander, sowing the fields with camel-drawn plows.

sentences.zh: 其可汗常樓居，妻號天公主，其國相號媚祿都督。

translations.literal: Their khan usually lived in a tower; his wife was called the Heavenly Princess, and the state minister was titled the Meilu commander.
translations.idiomatic: The khan lived in a tower dwelling; his consort was called the Heavenly Princess, and his chief minister bore the title Meilu Commander.

sentences.zh: 見可汗，則去帽被髮而入以爲禮。

translations.literal: To see the khan one removed one's cap, let down one's hair, and entered—that was the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To approach the khan one removed one's cap, unbound one's hair, and entered bareheaded—that was the proper rite.

sentences.zh: 婦人總發爲髻，高五六寸，以紅絹囊之；

translations.literal: Women bound their hair in a topknot five or six inches high and wrapped it in red silk;
translations.idiomatic: Women bound their hair into a topknot five or six inches high and wrapped it in red silk;

sentences.zh: 既嫁，則加氈帽。

translations.literal: after marriage they added a felt cap.
translations.idiomatic: after marriage they added a felt cap.

sentences.zh: 又有別族號龍家，其俗與回紇小異。

translations.literal: There was also a separate people called the Dragon Clan, whose customs differed slightly from the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: A separate people called the Dragon Clan lived among them, with customs slightly different from the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，回鶻來獻白鶻一聯，明宗命解緤放之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing the Uyghurs presented a pair of white swans; Mingzong ordered them unbound and released.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing the Uyghurs presented a pair of white swans, which Mingzong ordered released.

sentences.zh: 自明宗時，常以馬市中國，其所齎寶玉皆屬縣官，而民犯禁爲市者輒罪之。

translations.literal: From Mingzong's time they regularly traded horses in China; the jade and gems they brought all belonged to the state treasury, and commoners who violated the ban to trade were punished.
translations.idiomatic: From Mingzong's reign they regularly sold horses in China. The jade they brought was reserved for the state, and private trade was punished.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時除其禁，民得與回鶻私市，玉價由此倍賤。

translations.literal: In the time of Zhou Emperor Taizu the ban was lifted; the people could trade privately with the Uyghurs, and the price of jade thereby fell by half.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Taizu lifted the ban, allowing private trade with the Uyghurs, and the price of jade fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，來獻玉，世宗曰：「玉雖寶而無益。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era they came presenting jade; Shizong said, "Though jade is precious, it is of no use."
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era they presented jade. Shizong said, "Jade may be precious, but it serves no practical purpose."

sentences.zh: 」卻之。

translations.literal: He declined it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 于闐，國地、君世、物俗見於唐。

translations.literal: Khotan—its territory, rulers, and customs—are recorded in Tang histories.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan's lands, rulers, and customs were recorded in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 五代亂世，中國多故，不能撫來四夷。

translations.literal: In the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties China had many troubles and could not win over the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: During the chaotic Five Dynasties China was consumed by internal troubles and could not win over the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 其嘗自通於中國者僅以名見，其君世、終始，皆不可知。

translations.literal: Those who on their own had contact with China are known only by name; their rulers' genealogies and beginnings and ends are all unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Those who maintained contact appear only as names; the lineages and histories of their rulers are unknown.

sentences.zh: 而于闐尤遠，去京師萬里外。

translations.literal: Khotan was especially remote, more than ten thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan lay farthest of all, more than ten thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 其國西南近蔥嶺，與婆羅門爲鄰國，而相去猶三千餘里，南接吐蕃，西北至疏勒二千餘里。

translations.literal: Their state in the southwest neared the Onion Mountains and bordered the land of Brahmans, yet was still more than three thousand li distant; south it adjoined Tibet, and northwest to Shule was more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest it approached the Onion Mountains and lay three thousand li from Brahman lands. It bordered Tibet to the south and stood more than two thousand li northwest of Shule.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年，于闐國王李聖天遣使者馬繼榮來貢紅鹽、郁金、氂牛尾、玉灊等，晉遣供奉官張匡鄴假鴻臚卿，彰武軍節度判官高居誨爲判官，冊聖天爲大寶于闐國王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu of Jin the king of Khotan Li Shengtian sent the envoy Ma Jirong to offer tribute of red salt, turmeric, yak tails, jade felt, and the like; Jin sent the palace attendant Zhang Kuangye acting as director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, with Gao Juhui, judge of the Zhangwu military commission, as vice-commissioner, to invest Shengtian as king of Great Treasure Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu, King Li Shengtian of Khotan sent Ma Jirong with tribute of red salt, turmeric, yak tails, and jade felt. Jin dispatched palace attendant Zhang Kuangye as acting director of diplomatic reception, with Zhangwu judge Gao Juhui as vice-commissioner, to invest Shengtian as king of Great Treasure Khotan.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬十二月，匡鄴等自靈州行二歲至于闐，至七年冬乃還。

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month of winter Kuangye and the others set out from Lingzhou; after two years they reached Khotan, and in the winter of the seventh year they returned.
translations.idiomatic: They departed Lingzhou in the twelfth month of that winter, reached Khotan after two years on the road, and returned in the winter of the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 而居誨頗記其往復所見山川諸國，而不能道聖天世次也。

translations.literal: Gao Juhui recorded in detail the mountains, rivers, and states seen on the journey there and back, but could not relate Shengtian's genealogy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Juhui recorded the mountains, rivers, and kingdoms seen along the route, but could not trace Shengtian's lineage.

sentences.zh: 居誨記曰：「自靈州過黃河，行三十里，始涉沙入党項界，曰細腰沙、神點沙。

translations.literal: Gao Juhui's record says: "From Lingzhou crossing the Yellow River, after thirty li one first entered the sands into Tangut territory, called Narrow-Waist Sand and Spirit-Point Sand."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Juhui wrote: "From Lingzhou we crossed the Yellow River and, after thirty li, entered the sands of Tangut territory at Narrow-Waist Sand and Spirit-Point Sand."

sentences.zh: 至三公沙，宿月支都督帳。

translations.literal: Reaching Three-Lord Sand, they lodged at the tent of the Yuezhi commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Three-Lord Sand they lodged in the tent of the Yuezhi commander.

sentences.zh: 自此沙行四百餘里，至黑堡沙，沙尤廣，遂登沙嶺。

translations.literal: From there they traveled the sands more than four hundred li to Black Fortress Sand; the sands grew especially vast, and they then ascended Sand Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed four hundred li of sand to Black Fortress Sand, where the desert widened still further, then climbed Sand Ridge.

sentences.zh: 沙嶺，党項牙也，其酋曰撚崖天子。

translations.literal: Sand Ridge was the Tangut headquarters; their chief was called the Nianya Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Sand Ridge was the Tangut headquarters, ruled by a chief styled the Nianya Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 渡白亭河至涼州，自涼州西行五百里至甘州。

translations.literal: Crossing the Baiting River they reached Liangzhou; from Liangzhou west five hundred li to Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Baiting River to Liangzhou, then traveled five hundred li west to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 甘州，回鶻牙也。

translations.literal: Ganzhou was the Uyghur headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou was the Uyghur headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其南，山百餘里，漢小月支之故地也，有別族號鹿角山沙陀，雲硃耶氏之遺族也。

translations.literal: South of it, a hundred-odd li of mountains, was the old land of the Lesser Yuezhi of Han; there was a separate people called the Antler Mountain Shatuo, said to be remnants of the Zhuye clan.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li to the south lay the old homeland of the Lesser Yuezhi. A separate people called the Antler Mountain Shatuo lived there, said to be descendants of the Zhuye clan.

sentences.zh: 自甘州西，始涉磧。

translations.literal: West from Ganzhou they first entered the gravel desert.
translations.idiomatic: West of Ganzhou the gravel desert began.

sentences.zh: 磧無水，載水以行。

translations.literal: The desert had no water; they carried water to travel.
translations.idiomatic: The desert held no water, so they carried supplies to survive.

sentences.zh: 甘州人教晉使者作馬蹄木澀，木澀四竅，馬蹄亦鑿四竅而綴之，駝蹄則包以氂皮乃可行。

translations.literal: The people of Ganzhou taught the Jin envoys to make wooden hoof-grips: the grips had four holes, and horse hooves were also bored with four holes and fastened to them; camel hooves were wrapped in yak hide before they could travel.
translations.idiomatic: Locals taught the Jin envoys to fit wooden hoof grips with four holes, bored to match four holes drilled in each horse's hooves. Camel hooves had to be wrapped in yak hide before they could cross the desert.

sentences.zh: 西北五百里至肅州，渡金河，西百里出天門關，又西百里出玉門關，經吐蕃界。

translations.literal: Northwest five hundred li to Suzhou; crossing the Golden River, a hundred li west to exit Heaven's Gate Pass, another hundred li west to exit Jade Gate Pass, passing through Tibetan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li northwest lay Suzhou. They crossed the Golden River, passed Heaven's Gate a hundred li west, then Jade Gate another hundred li west, traveling through Tibetan lands.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃男子冠中國帽，婦人辮髪，戴瑟瑟珠，雲珠之好者，一珠易一良馬。

translations.literal: Tibetan men wore Chinese caps; women braided their hair and wore sese beads—it was said that the finest bead could be exchanged for one good horse.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan men wore Chinese-style caps. Women braided their hair and wore sese beads; the finest beads were said to trade for a good horse apiece.

sentences.zh: 西至瓜州、沙州，二州多中國人，聞晉使者來，其刺史曹元深等郊迎，問使者天子起居。

translations.literal: West to Guazhou and Shazhou; the two prefectures had many Chinese. Hearing the Jin envoys were coming, their prefects Cao Yuanshen and others met them in the suburbs and asked after the Son of Heaven's health.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west lay Guazhou and Shazhou, where many Chinese still lived. Prefect Cao Yuanshen and others rode out to greet the Jin envoys and inquire after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 瓜州南十里鳴沙山，雲冬夏殷殷有聲如雷，雲《禹貢》流沙也。

translations.literal: Ten li south of Guazhou was Echoing Sand Mountain; it was said that winter and summer it rumbled like thunder—it was said to be the drifting sands of the "Tribute of Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Ten li south of Guazhou stood Echoing Sand Mountain, which rumbled like thunder year-round and was identified with the drifting sands of the Tribute of Yu.

sentences.zh: 又東南十里三危山，雲三苗之所竄也。

translations.literal: Another ten li southeast was Three Perils Mountain; it was said to be where the Three Miao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li farther southeast lay Three Perils Mountain, said to be where the Three Miao had fled.

sentences.zh: 其西，渡都鄉河曰陽關。

translations.literal: West of it, crossing the Duxiang River was called Yang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: West of there, crossing the Duxiang River, lay Yang Pass.

sentences.zh: 沙州西曰仲雲，其牙帳居胡盧磧。

translations.literal: West of Shazhou was called Zhongyun; their headquarters dwelt at Hulu Desert.
translations.idiomatic: West of Shazhou lay Zhongyun, whose headquarters stood in the Hulu Desert.

sentences.zh: 雲仲雲者，小月支之遺種也，其人勇而好戰，瓜、沙之人皆憚之。

translations.literal: It was said the Zhongyun were remnants of the Lesser Yuezhi; their people were brave and loved battle, and the people of Guazhou and Shazhou all feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongyun were said to be remnants of the Lesser Yuezhi, fierce warriors whom the people of Guazhou and Shazhou feared.

sentences.zh: 胡盧磧，漢明帝時征匈奴，屯田于吾盧，蓋其地也。

translations.literal: Hulu Desert: in Emperor Ming of Han's campaign against the Xiongnu, garrison farming was established at Wulu—this was likely that place.
translations.idiomatic: The Hulu Desert was likely the site where Emperor Ming of Han had garrisoned troops at Wulu during his campaigns against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 地無水而嘗寒多雪，每天暖雪銷，乃得水。

translations.literal: The land had no water and was often cold with heavy snow; only when the weather warmed and the snow melted could water be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The land had no standing water and was bitterly cold and snowy. Water appeared only when the sun melted the snow.

sentences.zh: 匡鄴等西行入仲雲界，至大屯城，仲雲遣宰相四人、都督三十七人候晉使者，匡鄴等以詔書慰諭之，皆東向拜。

translations.literal: Kuangye and the others traveled west into Zhongyun territory to Great Garrison City; Zhongyun sent four chancellors and thirty-seven commanders to await the Jin envoys; Kuangye and the others consoled them with the imperial edict, and all bowed facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangye's party entered Zhongyun territory as far as Great Garrison City. Four Zhongyun chancellors and thirty-seven commanders came to meet them. Kuangye read the imperial edict of consolation, and all bowed toward the east.

sentences.zh: 自仲雲界西，始涉𨢑磧，無水，掘地得濕沙，人置之胸以止渴。

translations.literal: West from Zhongyun territory they first entered the salt desert; there was no water; digging the ground yielded damp sand, which men placed against their chests to quench thirst.
translations.idiomatic: West of Zhongyun lay the salt desert without water. Travelers dug up damp sand and pressed it to their chests to slake their thirst.

sentences.zh: 又西，渡陷河，伐檉置水中乃渡，不然則陷。

translations.literal: Farther west they crossed the Sinking River; they felled tamarisk and laid it in the water before crossing—otherwise they would sink in.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west they crossed the Sinking River by laying cut tamarisk branches in the water; without that precaution travelers sank in.

sentences.zh: 又西，至紺州。

translations.literal: Farther west to Indigo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Still farther west they reached Indigo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紺州，于闐所置也，在沙州西南，雲去京師九千五百里矣。

translations.literal: Indigo Prefecture was established by Khotan, southwest of Shazhou; it was said to be nine thousand five hundred li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Indigo Prefecture, founded by Khotan southwest of Shazhou, was said to lie nine thousand five hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 又行二日至安軍州，遂至于闐。

translations.literal: After two more days' travel to Anjun Prefecture, they then reached Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they reached Anjun Prefecture, and then Khotan itself.

sentences.zh: 聖天衣冠如中國，其殿皆東向，曰金冊殿，有樓曰七鳳樓。

translations.literal: Shengtian's dress was like China's; his halls all faced east, called the Golden Book Hall, with a tower called the Seven Phoenix Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Shengtian dressed in Chinese style. His halls faced east, including the Golden Book Hall and the Seven Phoenix Tower.

sentences.zh: 以蒲桃爲酒，又有紫酒、青酒，不知其所釀，而味尤美。

translations.literal: They made wine from grapes; there were also purple wine and green wine—unknown what they were brewed from, but the taste was especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: They made wine from grapes, along with purple and green wines of unknown ingredients whose flavor was especially fine.

sentences.zh: 其食，粳沃以蜜，粟沃以酪。

translations.literal: Their food: glutinous rice moistened with honey, millet moistened with curds.
translations.idiomatic: They ate glutinous rice softened with honey and millet softened with curds.

sentences.zh: 其衣布帛。

translations.literal: They wore cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: They dressed in cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 有園圃花木。

translations.literal: They had gardens and flowering trees.
translations.idiomatic: They kept gardens and flowering trees.

sentences.zh: 俗喜鬼神而好佛。

translations.literal: Their custom favored spirits and ghosts and loved Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: They venerated spirits and were devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 聖天居處，嘗以紫衣僧五十人列侍，其年號同慶二十九年。

translations.literal: At Shengtian's residence fifty purple-robed monks were once arrayed in attendance; his reign era was Tongqing, year twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty purple-robed monks stood in attendance at Shengtian's court. His reign era was Tongqing, in its twenty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 其國東南曰銀州、盧州、湄州，其南千三百里曰玉州，雲漢張騫所窮河源出于闐，而山多玉者此山也。

translations.literal: Southeast of their state were Yinzhou, Luzhou, and Meizhou; thirteen hundred li south was Yuzhou—it was said that the source of the river Zhang Qian of Han traced to its end issued from Khotan, and this was the mountain rich in jade.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast lay Yinzhou, Luzhou, and Meizhou. Thirteen hundred li south stood Yuzhou, on the mountain said to be the jade-rich source of the river whose upper reaches Zhang Qian of Han had traced to its end in Khotan.

sentences.zh: 」其河源所出，至于闐分爲三：東曰白玉河，西曰綠玉河，又西曰烏玉河。

translations.literal: Where the river source issued, reaching Khotan it divided into three: east was the White Jade River, west the Green Jade River, and farther west the Black Jade River.
translations.idiomatic: At its source the river split into three branches in Khotan: the White Jade River to the east, the Green Jade River to the west, and the Black Jade River farther west.

sentences.zh: 三河皆有玉而色異，每歲秋水涸，國王撈玉于河，然後國人得撈玉。

translations.literal: All three rivers had jade but of different colors; each year when the autumn waters dried, the king gathered jade from the rivers, and only then could the people gather jade.
translations.idiomatic: Each river yielded jade of a different color. Each autumn, when the waters fell, the king gathered jade first; only afterward could the people do the same.

sentences.zh: 自靈州渡黃河至于闐，往往見吐蕃族帳，而于闐常與吐蕃相攻劫。

translations.literal: From Lingzhou crossing the Yellow River to Khotan one often saw Tibetan tribal tents, and Khotan frequently raided and fought with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: From Lingzhou to Khotan along the Yellow River route, Tibetan encampments were common, and Khotan and Tibet raided each other repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 匡鄴等至于闐，聖天頗責誚之，以邀誓約。

translations.literal: When Kuangye and the others reached Khotan, Shengtian rebuked them sharply to secure a sworn pact.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuangye's party arrived, Shengtian rebuked them harshly to extract a sworn alliance.

sentences.zh: 匡鄴等還，聖天又遣都督劉再升獻玉千斤及玉印、降魔杵等。

translations.literal: When Kuangye and the others returned, Shengtian again sent the commander Liu Zaisheng to present a thousand jin of jade, a jade seal, a demon-subduing staff, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: On their return Shengtian sent Commander Liu Zaisheng with a thousand jin of jade, a jade seal, a demon-subduing staff, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐元年，又遣使者王知鐸來。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyou of Han he again sent the envoy Wang Zhiduo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Later Han's Qianyou reign he sent another envoy, Wang Zhiduo.

sentences.zh: 高麗，本扶餘人之別種也。

translations.literal: Goryeo was originally a separate branch of the Fuyu people.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo was originally an offshoot of the Fuyu people.

sentences.zh: 其國地、君世見於唐，比他夷狄有姓氏，而其官號略可曉其義。

translations.literal: Their territory and rulers are recorded in Tang; unlike other barbarians they had surnames, and their official titles' meanings can largely be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands and rulers appear in the Tang histories. Unlike other frontier peoples they used surnames, and their official titles are largely intelligible.

sentences.zh: 當唐之末，其王姓高氏。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang their king bore the surname Gao.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Tang their royal house bore the surname Gao.

sentences.zh: 同光元年，遣使廣評侍郎韓申一、副使春部少卿樸岩來，而其國王姓名，史失不紀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongguang they sent the envoy Vice Director of Broad Evaluation Han Shenyi and the vice-envoy Junior Director of the Spring Office Piao Yan, but their king's name is lost in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongguang they sent envoy Han Shenyi and vice-envoy Piao Yan, but the king's name was not recorded.

sentences.zh: 至長興三年，權知國事王建遣使者來，明宗乃拜建玄菟州都督，充大義軍使，封高麗國王。

translations.literal: By the third year of Changxing Wang Jian, acting in state affairs, sent envoys; Mingzong then appointed Jian commander of Xuantu Prefecture, made him commissioner of the Dayi Army, and enfeoffed him as king of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing, Wang Jian, acting ruler, sent envoys. Mingzong appointed him commander of Xuantu, commissioner of the Dayi Army, and king of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 建，高麗大族也。

translations.literal: Jian was of a great Goryeo clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian came from a leading Goryeo clan.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，建卒，子武立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun Jian died and his son Wu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jian died in the second year of Kaiyun and was succeeded by his son Wu.

sentences.zh: 乾祐四年，武卒，子昭立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianyou Wu died and his son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu died in the fourth year of Qianyou and was succeeded by his son Zhao.

sentences.zh: 王氏三世，終五代常來朝貢，其立也必請命中國，中國常優答之。

translations.literal: The Wang house for three generations throughout the Five Dynasties came regularly with tribute; on succession they always requested investiture from China, and China always responded generously.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of the Wang house sent tribute throughout the Five Dynasties, always seeking Chinese investiture on succession, which the court generously granted.

sentences.zh: 其地產銅、銀，周世宗時，遣尚書水部員外郎韓彥卿以帛數千匹市銅於高麗以鑄鐵。

translations.literal: Their land produced copper and silver; in Emperor Shizong's time he sent Han Yanqing, vice director of the Water Office in the Ministry of Works, with several thousand bolts of silk to buy copper in Goryeo for casting iron.
translations.idiomatic: Their country produced copper and silver. Shizong sent Han Yanqing of the Ministry of Works with thousands of bolts of silk to buy Goryeo copper for iron casting.

sentences.zh: 六年，昭遣使者貢黃銅五萬斤。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhao sent envoys offering fifty thousand jin of yellow copper.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhao sent fifty thousand jin of brass as tribute.

sentences.zh: 高麗俗知文字，喜讀書，昭進《別敘孝經》一卷、《越王新義》八卷、《皇靈孝經》一卷、《孝經雌圖》一卷。

translations.literal: Goryeo custom knew writing and loved books; Zhao presented one scroll of Separate Narrative to the Classic of Filial Piety, eight scrolls of New Meaning of the King of Yue, one scroll of Imperial Spirit Classic of Filial Piety, and one scroll of Yin Chart of the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo were literate and fond of learning. Zhao presented Separate Narrative to the Classic of Filial Piety, New Meaning of the King of Yue in eight scrolls, Imperial Spirit Classic of Filial Piety, and Yin Chart of the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 《別敘》，敘孔子所生及弟子事蹟；

translations.literal: Separate Narrative narrated where Confucius was born and the deeds of his disciples;
translations.idiomatic: Separate Narrative recounted Confucius's birthplace and the deeds of his disciples;

sentences.zh: 《越王新義》，以「越王」爲問目，若今「正義」；

translations.literal: New Meaning of the King of Yue took "King of Yue" as the topic of inquiry, like today's "Correct Meaning";
translations.idiomatic: New Meaning of the King of Yue used "King of Yue" as its interpretive frame, like modern commentaries;

sentences.zh: 《皇靈》，述延年辟穀；

translations.literal: Imperial Spirit described Yan Nian's grain avoidance;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Spirit described Yan Nian's fasting regimen;

sentences.zh: 《雌圖》，載日食、星變。

translations.literal: Yin Chart recorded solar eclipses and stellar anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chart recorded solar eclipses and unusual stars.

sentences.zh: 皆不經之說。

translations.literal: All were unorthodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: All were unorthodox works.
