sentences.zh: 渤海，本號靺鞨，高麗之別種也。

translations.literal: Bohai was originally called Mohe, a separate branch of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai, originally called Mohe, was an offshoot of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 唐高宗滅高麗，徙其人散處中國，置安東都護府於平壤以統治之。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Gaozong destroyed Goryeo, relocated its people scattered through China, and established the Protectorate General of Andong at Pyongyang to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong of Tang destroyed Goryeo, resettled its people across China, and placed the Protectorate General of Andong at Pyongyang to rule the region.

sentences.zh: 武后時，契丹攻北邊，高麗別種大乞乞仲象與靺鞨酋長乞四比羽走遼東，分王高麗故地，武后遣將擊殺乞四比羽，而乞乞仲象亦病死。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time the Khitan attacked the northern frontier; the Goryeo offshoot Daqiqizhongxiang and the Mohe chief Qisibiyu fled to Liaodong and divided rule of old Goryeo lands; Wu sent generals who killed Qisibiyu, and Qiqi Zhongxiang also died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu the Khitan raided the north. The Goryeo splinter leader Daqiqizhongxiang and Mohe chief Qisibiyu fled to Liaodong and divided the old Goryeo lands between them. Wu's generals killed Qisibiyu, and Zhongxiang soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 仲象子祚榮立，因並有比羽之衆，其衆四十萬人，據挹婁，臣于唐。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang's son Zuorong succeeded, thereby also absorbing Biyu's followers; his people numbered four hundred thousand, he held Yilou, and submitted to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang's son Zuorong succeeded him, absorbed Biyu's followers, and commanded four hundred thousand people at Yilou before submitting to Tang.

sentences.zh: 至中宗時，置忽汗州，以祚榮爲都督，封渤海郡王，其後世遂號渤海。

translations.literal: By Emperor Zhongzong's time Hohan Prefecture was established, Zuorong made commander, and enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai Commandery; later generations thus took the name Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong the court established Hohan Prefecture, made Zuorong its commander, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Bohai. Later generations took Bohai as their name.

sentences.zh: 其貴族姓大氏，開平元年，國王大諲撰遣使者來，訖顯德常來朝貢。

translations.literal: Their nobles bore the surname Da; in the first year of Kaiping the king Da Yinzuan sent envoys, and down to Xiande they came regularly with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Their nobility bore the surname Da. King Da Yinzuan sent envoys in the first year of Kaiping, and tribute missions continued through the Xiande era.

sentences.zh: 其國土物產，與高麗同。

translations.literal: Their country's products were the same as Goryeo's.
translations.idiomatic: Their products were much the same as Goryeo's.

sentences.zh: 諲撰世次、立卒，史失其紀。

translations.literal: Yinzuan's genealogy, rise, and death are lost in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzuan's lineage and reign dates have been lost.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨

translations.literal: Heishui Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Heishui Mohe.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨，本號勿吉。

translations.literal: Heishui Mohe were originally called Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe were originally known as the Wuji.

sentences.zh: 當後魏時見中國。

translations.literal: They appeared in China during the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They appear in Chinese records from the Northern Wei period.

sentences.zh: 其國，東至海，南界高麗，西接突厥，北鄰室韋，蓋肅慎氏之地也。

translations.literal: Their country reached the sea in the east, bordered Goryeo in the south, adjoined the Turks in the west, and neighbored the Shiwei in the north—it was the land of the Sushen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Their country reached the sea in the east, bordered Goryeo in the south, met the Turks in the west, and neighbored the Shiwei in the north—the ancient land of the Sushen.

sentences.zh: 其衆分爲數十部，而黑水靺鞨最處其北，尤勁悍，無文字之記。

translations.literal: Their people were divided into several tens of divisions; the Heishui Mohe were farthest north and especially fierce, with no written records.
translations.idiomatic: They were divided into dozens of tribes. The Heishui Mohe lived farthest north, were especially fierce, and left no written records.

sentences.zh: 其兵，角弓、楛矢。

translations.literal: Their weapons were horn bows and wooden arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They fought with horn bows and wooden-shafted arrows.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，黑水兀兒遣使者來，其後常來朝貢，自登州泛海出青州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang the Heishui Wuer sent envoys; afterward they came regularly with tribute, sailing from Dengzhou across the sea to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongguang the Heishui chief Wuer sent envoys. Thereafter tribute missions sailed from Dengzhou across the sea to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，黑水胡獨鹿亦遣使來。

translations.literal: The next year the Heishui Hudulu also sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Heishui chief Hudulu sent envoys as well.

sentences.zh: 兀兒、胡獨鹿若其兩部酋長，各以使來。

translations.literal: Wuer and Hudulu were likely chiefs of two divisions, each sending envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wuer and Hudulu were apparently chiefs of two divisions, each sending his own mission.

sentences.zh: 而其部族、世次、立卒，史皆失其紀。

translations.literal: But their tribes, genealogies, rises, and deaths are all lost in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribal affiliations, genealogies, and reign dates have all been lost.

sentences.zh: 至長興三年，胡獨鹿卒，子桃李花立，嘗請命中國，後遂不復見云。

translations.literal: By the third year of Changxing Hudulu died and his son Taolihua succeeded; he once requested investiture from China, but afterward was seen no more.
translations.idiomatic: Hudulu died in the third year of Changxing and was succeeded by his son Taolihua, who once sought Chinese investiture but thereafter disappears from the record.

sentences.zh: 南詔蠻

translations.literal: Nanzhao Man.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 南詔蠻，見於唐。

translations.literal: Nanzhao Man appear in Tang records.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao appears in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 其國在漢故永昌郡之東、姚州之西。

translations.literal: Their state lay east of Han's old Yongchang Commandery and west of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Their kingdom lay east of the old Han commandery of Yongchang and west of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗幸蜀，募能使南詔者，得宗室子李龜年及徐虎、虎侄藹，乃以龜年爲使，虎爲副，藹爲判官，使南詔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong went to Shu he recruited men who could deal with Nanzhao, finding the imperial clansman Li Guinian and Xu Hu and Hu's nephew Ai; he made Guinian envoy, Hu vice-envoy, and Ai judge, and sent them to Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong fled to Shu he sought men who could treat with Nanzhao and found the clansman Li Guinian, Xu Hu, and Hu's nephew Ai. Guinian was made envoy, Hu vice-envoy, and Ai judge of the mission.

sentences.zh: 南詔所居曰苴絺城，龜年等不至苴絺，至善闡，得其要約與唐爲甥舅。

translations.literal: Nanzhao's seat was called Juzhi City; Guinian and the others did not reach Juzhi but arrived at Shanchan and secured a pact making Tang and Nanzhao uncle and nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao's capital was Juzhi City. Guinian's party did not reach it but stopped at Shanchan and secured a pact of uncle-nephew kinship with Tang.

sentences.zh: 僖宗許以安化公主妻之，南詔大喜，遣人隨龜年求公主。

translations.literal: Xizong promised the Princess of Anhua as wife; Nanzhao was greatly pleased and sent men with Guinian to request the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong promised the Princess of Anhua in marriage. Nanzhao rejoiced and sent men with Guinian to claim her.

sentences.zh: 已而黃巢敗，收復長安，僖宗東還，乃止。

translations.literal: Soon Huang Chao was defeated, Chang'an recovered, and Xizong returned east—the matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao fell, Chang'an was recovered, and Xizong returned east, the marriage plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，魏王繼岌及郭崇韜等破蜀，得王衍時所俘南詔蠻數十人，又得徐藹，自言嘗使南詔，乃矯詔還其所俘，遣藹等持金帛招撫南詔，諭以威德，南詔不納。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang Prince Jiji of Wei and Guo Chongtao and others conquered Shu, obtaining several tens of Nanzhao captives from Wang Yan's time, and also Xu Ai, who said he had once been envoy to Nanzhao; they forged an edict to return the captives and sent Ai and others with gold and silk to win over Nanzhao, instructing them in power and virtue, but Nanzhao did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang, Prince Jiji and Guo Chongtao conquered Shu and recovered dozens of Nanzhao captives taken under Wang Yan, along with Xu Ai, who claimed prior service as envoy. They forged an edict returning the captives and sent Ai with gold and silk to win Nanzhao over, but Nanzhao refused.

sentences.zh: 至明宗時，巂州山后兩林百蠻都鬼主、右武衛大將軍李卑晚，遣大鬼主傅能何華來朝貢，明宗拜卑晚甯遠將軍，又以大渡河南山前邛州六姓都鬼主懷安郡王勿定摽莎爲定遠將軍。

translations.literal: By Mingzong's time the chief ghost-lord of the Two Forests Hundred Barbarians behind Mount Xizhou, General of the Right Martial Guard Li Beiwan, sent the great ghost-lord Fu Nenghua to offer tribute; Mingzong appointed Beiwan General of Pacifying the Distance, and also made the chief ghost-lord of the Six Clans south of the Dadu River in Qiongzhou, Prince of Huai'an Commandery Wuding Biaosha, General of Fixing the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong, Li Beiwan, chief of the Two Forests Hundred Barbarians of Xizhou and general of the Right Martial Guard, sent Great Ghost-Lord Fu Nenghua with tribute. Mingzong made Beiwan General of Pacifying the Distance and Wuding Biaosha, Six-Clans ghost-lord south of the Dadu River, General of Fixing the Distance.

sentences.zh: 明年遣左金吾衛將軍烏昭遠爲入蠻國信使，昭遠不能達而還。

translations.literal: The next year he sent Wu Zhaoyuan, general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, as credentialed envoy into the Man lands; Zhaoyuan could not reach them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu Zhaoyuan of the Left Golden Crow Guard was sent as credentialed envoy to the Man lands but could not get through and returned.

sentences.zh: 牂牁蠻，在辰州西千五百里，以耕植爲生，而無城郭聚落，有所攻擊，則相屯聚。

translations.literal: The Zhangke Man, fifteen hundred li west of Chenzhou, lived by farming but had no walled towns or settlements; when there was an attack they gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangke Man lived fifteen hundred li west of Chenzhou by agriculture, without walled towns. When threatened they gathered for defense.

sentences.zh: 刻木爲契。

translations.literal: They carved wood for contracts.
translations.idiomatic: They recorded agreements by carving wood.

sentences.zh: 其首領姓謝氏，其名見於唐。

translations.literal: Their chiefs bore the surname Xie; their names appear in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs bore the surname Xie, recorded in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 至天成二年嘗一至，其使者曰清州八郡刺史宋朝化，冠帶如中國，貢草豆蔻二萬個、硃砂五百兩、蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: By the second year of Tiancheng they came once; their envoy was called Prefect of the Eight Commanderies of Qingzhou Song Chaohua, wearing cap and belt like China, offering twenty thousand cardamom pods, five hundred liang of cinnabar, and two hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng they came once. Their envoy, styled Prefect Song Chaohua of Qingzhou's eight commanderies, dressed in Chinese cap and belt and offered twenty thousand cardamom pods, five hundred liang of cinnabar, and two hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 昆明，在黔州西南三千里外，地產羊馬。

translations.literal: Kunming lay three thousand li southwest of Qianzhou; the land produced sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kunming lay three thousand li southwest of Qianzhou and produced sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 其人椎髻、跣足、披氈，其首領披虎皮。

translations.literal: Their people wore topknots, went barefoot, and draped felt; their chiefs wore tiger skins.
translations.idiomatic: They wore topknots, went barefoot, and wrapped themselves in felt; their chiefs wore tiger pelts.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，嘗一至，其首領號昆明大鬼主，羅殿王、普露靜王九部落，各遣使者來，使者號若土，附牂牁以來。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng they came once; their chief was styled Great Ghost-Lord of Kunming; the King of Luodian, King of Pulujing, and nine tribes each sent envoys styled Ruotu, arriving attached to the Zhangke mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng they came once. Their chief styled himself Great Ghost-Lord of Kunming. The kings of Luodian and Pulujing and nine tribes each sent envoys called Ruotu, arriving with the Zhangke mission.

sentences.zh: 占城，在西南海上。

translations.literal: Champa lay on the southwestern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Champa lay on the southwestern seas.

sentences.zh: 其地方千里，東至海，西至雲南，南鄰真腦，北抵驩州。

translations.literal: Their territory was a thousand li square, reaching the sea in the east, Yunnan in the west, bordering Zhennao in the south, and Huanzhou in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory spanned a thousand li, reaching the sea in the east, Yunnan in the west, Zhennao in the south, and Huanzhou in the north.

sentences.zh: 其人，俗與大食同。

translations.literal: Their people's customs were the same as those of the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs resembled those of the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 其乘，象、馬；

translations.literal: Their mounts were elephants and horses;
translations.idiomatic: They rode elephants and horses;

sentences.zh: 其食，稻米、水兕、山羊。

translations.literal: their food was rice, river rhinoceros, and mountain goats.
translations.idiomatic: their food was rice, river rhinoceros, and mountain goats.

sentences.zh: 鳥獸之奇，犀、孔雀。

translations.literal: Among their strange birds and beasts were rhinoceroses and peacocks.
translations.idiomatic: Notable among their fauna were rhinoceroses and peacocks.

sentences.zh: 自前世未嘗通中國。

translations.literal: From previous ages they had never had contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: No earlier dynasty had had contact with them.

sentences.zh: 顯德五年，其國王因德漫遣使者莆訶散來，貢猛火油八十四瓶、薔薇水十五瓶，其表以貝多葉書之，以香木爲函。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiande their king Yindeman sent the envoy Puhesan, offering eighty-four bottles of fierce fire oil and fifteen bottles of rose water; the memorial was written on pattra leaves and the case made of fragrant wood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiande King Yindeman sent envoy Puhesan with eighty-four bottles of Greek fire and fifteen of rose water. The memorial was written on pattra leaves in a case of fragrant wood.

sentences.zh: 猛火油以灑物，得水則出火。

translations.literal: Fierce fire oil, when sprinkled on things, burst into flame on contact with water.
translations.idiomatic: Greek fire burst into flame when sprinkled on objects and touched by water.

sentences.zh: 薔薇水，雲得自西域，以灑衣，雖敝而香不滅。

translations.literal: Rose water, said to come from the Western Regions, when sprinkled on clothes kept its fragrance even when worn out.
translations.idiomatic: Rose water, said to come from the Western Regions, perfumed clothing so that the scent lingered even when the cloth was worn threadbare.

sentences.zh: 五代，四夷見中國者，遠不過于闐、占城。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties, among the four barbarians who appeared in China, none came from farther than Khotan and Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Among the frontier peoples who reached China during the Five Dynasties, none came from farther than Khotan and Champa.

sentences.zh: 史之所紀，其西北頗詳，而東南尤略，蓋其遠而罕至，且不爲中國利害云。

translations.literal: What the histories record is rather detailed for the northwest but especially sparse for the southeast—likely because those lands were distant and rarely reached, and were of no profit or harm to China.
translations.idiomatic: The histories are fairly detailed on the northwest but especially thin on the southeast, no doubt because those lands were remote, seldom visited, and of little consequence to China.
